analysis:
This batch contains only test changes. The production code they exercise was not supplied.

ClusterOwnerServingTests.swift (head 68-127) adds two tests:
- One test covers a new ClusterPublicModels declaration. A model the owner declared public (GLM-5.3-Flash, Qwen3.8-27B) gets the 'qualified for public traffic' line in its declared pipeline and tensor-parallel families even without a passing qualification record. Head 82-84 checks this. A different artifact SHA, an undeclared family or an undeclared model stays notYetQualified (head 86-92, 107).
- The other test checks that a placement decoding with the speculative tensor assistant is 'not offered for public traffic' (head 121-125).
- Existing tests now pass publicModels: [] so that records alone decide (head 132-138). ClusterPairServingDecisionsTests head 157-158 does the same.

Security relevance: the tests suggest a production change where an owner-side declaration, not passing parity records, can mark families as publicly qualified. In head 77 the qualified string says the coordinator's parity qualification still decides each placement. If that holds, the provider-side line is advisory display text.

The integration pass should verify in the unseen ClusterPairServingGrants/ClusterPublicModels sources whether the declaration only changes the status line or also changes:
- the public grant (grant()/publicGrant families);
- the provider's advertised capabilities;
- coordinator-facing offers that could route public consumer traffic (A-001) to unqualified sharded placements.

This relates to T-007/T-027/T-054-style correctness/qualification concerns and the A-017 qualification contract. The tests show ownerServing exposes declaredFamilies (head 98), but whether publicGrant changes for declared models is not tested here.

The assistant exclusion should be confirmed as enforced at offer time, not only in display text.

No concrete regression is visible in test-only evidence.
